suggestion: Reject (or explicitly warn and refuse) when version > CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION.

title: Pre-migration database and index-metadata backups accumulate forever
description: Every migration run copies full DB (conn.backup) plus all indices/*.json metadata into backups/, nothing ever deletes old backups. Copy happens whenever user_version < CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION (including repeated failed attempts which restore and retry on next launch), so a flapping migration loop creates unbounded series of full database copies.
evidence:
let path = backup_dir.join(format!("biturbo-pre-v{}-{}.db", CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION, stamp));
conn.backup(DatabaseName::Main, &path, None)?;
suggestion: Retain only last N pre-migration backups (delete older after successful migration commit).

title: replace_all publishes an empty index before repopulating and persists partial state on error
description: replace_all resets Inner to fresh empty index under lock, releases, re-acquires in add_batch. Between the two acquisitions concurrent searches observe empty index (recall returns nothing mid-rebuild); if add_batch fails partway the index left partially populated with old contents gone; mark_dirty already set so debounced flusher persists partial state to disk. Recovery depends on repair being triggered later by digest mismatch.
suggestion: Build replacement Inner completely off to the side, then swap in under single lock; on error keep previous Inner intact.

title: Sanitize project id to block path traversal in index file paths
description:
create_project accepts an arbitrary caller-supplied id (the MCP create_project tool passes args.id straight through) and never validates it. project::delete builds filesystem paths with format!("{id}...") joined onto data_dir/indices, so an id like '../../Users/victim/file' escapes the directory: delete creates '{id}.mutation.lock' at an arbitrary path (OpenOptions create+write) and removes '{id}.tvim'/'{id}.uidmap.json' wherever such files exist. The MCP server is driven by LLM agents, so a prompt-injected agent gains an arbitrary file-create/delete primitive outside the data dir.

**Merged finding:** Also flagged from the persistence.rs angle: the same unsanitized id reaches {project_id}.mutation.lock paths in replay_index_mutations (persistence.rs:71-74).
evidence:
let id = input.id.unwrap_or_else(|| slugify(&input.name));  // no validation
...
.join(format!("{id}.mutation.lock")),
suggestion: Validate ids against ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$ in project::create (and defensively in delete/get), or key filenames off the numeric rowid.

title: Stop sending JSON-RPC responses to notification messages
description: dispatch() answers every inbound message including notifications (messages without id). 'notifications/initialized' returns json!({}) — not even a valid JSON-RPC object — and every other notification falls into the catch-all arm emitting a -32601 error response with id null. JSON-RPC 2.0 forbids replying to notifications; strict clients can error or mis-correlate replies.
evidence:
"notifications/initialized" => json!({}),
_ => json!({ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": id, "error": { "code": -32601, ... } })
suggestion: When req.id.is_none(), do not write any response: handle known notifications explicitly and drop unknown ones silently.

title: Run blocking tools off the sequential dispatch loop
description: The stdio loop awaits dispatch() inline, so requests are strictly serialized. Heavy synchronous tools (ingest_project, consolidate, import_folder, export_memories) execute directly on the async task. While one large ingest runs, the server cannot answer ping, operation_status, or cancel_operation: wire-level cancellation of long operations is impossible and client timeouts fire.
evidence:
let response = match serde_json::from_str::<JsonRpcRequest>(trimmed) {
    Ok(req) => dispatch(&state, req).await,
suggestion: Spawn each request as a tokio task (JSON-RPC allows out-of-order responses) or run blocking tools via tokio::task::spawn_blocking; serialize stdout writes behind a mutex.

title: Disable the file watcher when deleting a project
description: project::delete removes memories, the project row, and index files, but never calls io::disable_watch and never removes the WATCHERS registry entry. A deleted-but-watched project keeps its notify watcher alive: every filesystem event re-triggers a watch ingest that fails at project::get, spamming errors; if a new project is later created with the same id, the stale watcher silently ingests the OLD root_path into the NEW project.
evidence:
// delete body only: flush_all_indices / indices.write().remove / remove_file / db.write(DELETE...)
// io.rs:205: WATCHERS.write().remove(project_id);  <- only inside disable_watch
suggestion: Call crate::io::disable_watch(state, id) inside project::delete before dropping the rows.

title: Add a single-instance guard for the desktop app
description: run() registers no single-instance plugin (tauri-plugin-single-instance absent from Cargo.toml). Launching biTurbo twice yields two full AppState processes over the same SQLite DB and indices dir: duplicate tray icons, two consolidate schedulers, two debounced index flushers rewriting the same .tvim files where last-writer-wins loses vectors.
evidence:
.plugin(tauri_plugin_autostart::Builder::new().build())
.plugin(tauri_plugin_shell::init())
... // no single-instance plugin
suggestion: Add tauri-plugin-single-instance as the first plugin, focusing the existing window on second launch.

title: Clamp the list tool limit to prevent unbounded queries
description:
The list handler passes limit raw into memory::list which interpolates it as i64 into SQL LIMIT with no clamp. limit=9223372036854775808 wraps to i64::MIN; SQLite treats negative LIMIT as no limit, serializing the entire memories table into one JSON response (memory spike, hung connection).

**Merged finding:** Both the MCP `list` tool and the IPC `list_memories` command forward unclamped limits into SQL LIMIT; negative/huge values mean unbounded scans. Fix once inside memory::list and clamp at both boundaries.
evidence: let limit = args.get("limit").and_then(|v| v.as_u64()).unwrap_or(50) as usize;
suggestion: Clamp in the handler (limit.clamp(1, 500), mirroring bounded_k) or clamp inside memory::list.

title: Spawn scheduler in the standalone MCP binary or hide consolidate_status
description: The GUI spawns the consolidate scheduler (lib.rs:105) but the standalone MCP binary never does, while still exposing consolidate_status. In MCP-only sessions the tool reports idle/never-run forever and background decay/dedup never happens unless the agent manually calls consolidate.
evidence: run_mcp_server_stdio().await   // no scheduler::spawn anywhere in main
suggestion: Spawn the scheduler on the opened AppState inside run_mcp_server_stdio, or document consolidate_status as GUI-only.

title: Validate submit_recall_feedback value instead of defaulting and wrapping
description: value defaults a missing/invalid value to +1 (unwrap_or(1)), silently recording positive feedback. Additionally `as i8` truncates: 256 becomes 0, 300 becomes 44, 1000 becomes -24 — out-of-range values flip or zero the feedback signal instead of being rejected, corrupting recall ranking.
evidence: let value = args.get("value").and_then(|v| v.as_i64()).unwrap_or(1) as i8;
suggestion: Return Invalid when value missing; accept only -1 or 1.

title: Reject agent names that slugify to an empty id
description: register_agent derives the primary key via slugify(name), which maps every non-alphanumeric-ASCII char to '-' and drops empty parts. A non-ASCII name yields id "" — all such agents collapse into one upserted ghost row with empty id. Returned AgentEntry always reports created_at=now even when upserting an existing row.
evidence:
let id = slugify(&name);
Ok(AgentEntry { id, name, kind, last_seen: now, created_at: now, meta })
suggestion: Error on empty slug (fall back to uuid), read back actual created_at after upsert.

title: Verify explicit project_id exists in resolve_project_id
description: An explicitly supplied project_id is returned without existence check, unlike remember/ingest paths which validate via require_project. search/recall_for_context with a typo'd id then return empty results ('no relevant memories') instead of an error, leading agents to wrongly conclude the project has no memories.
suggestion: Run project::get(state, pid) for the explicit-id branch and propagate NotFound.

title: Make .biTurbo projectName resolution deterministic on name collisions
description: Resolution queries 'WHERE name = ?1 OR id = ?1 LIMIT 1'. Two projects can share a name; LIMIT 1 picks an arbitrary row and recall rooted at a directory whose .biTurbo says projectName=X can attach to the wrong project, surfacing another project's memories as context.
evidence: "SELECT id FROM projects WHERE name = ?1 OR id = ?1 LIMIT 1"
suggestion: Prefer exact id match; on multiple name matches return ambiguity error listing candidates.

title: Try-lock queued operations before resuming them in a second process
description: Both GUI and every MCP binary instance call operations::resume_pending on the shared data dir. resume_pending spawns executors for every 'queued' row without try-locking the per-operation lock; executors use blocking lock_exclusive. Two processes starting simultaneously both spawn a thread for the same queued op — second blocks then re-runs the entire operation after the first finishes (duplicate work, doubled activity records). recover_interrupted already models the correct try-lock-and-skip pattern.
evidence: spawn_ingest(state.clone(), operation.id, project_id, root);  // no try_lock
suggestion: try_lock the operation lock in resume_pending before spawning; skip ops already claimed by a live process.

title: Guard export_memories output_path against overwriting arbitrary files
description: The MCP export_memories tool writes JSON to any caller-supplied output_path: create_dir_all's parent and unconditionally fs::write's, clobbering existing files. Exposed to LLM agents, this is an arbitrary-file-overwrite primitive reachable via prompt injection.
suggestion: Refuse to overwrite existing file unless explicit overwrite flag passed; confine exports beneath app data dir.

title: Drop the discarded inline instructions literal in initialize
description: The initialize arm embeds a large hand-written instructions string then immediately overwrites response["result"]["instructions"] with MCP_INSTRUCTIONS. Dead weight and drift hazard (two instruction texts to keep in sync).
evidence:
let mut response = ok(&id, json!({ ... "instructions": "## biTurbo Memory Layer — Instructions\n\n..." }));
response["result"]["instructions"] = Value::String(MCP_INSTRUCTIONS.into());
suggestion: Build the result once from MCP_INSTRUCTIONS only.

title: Refresh tray stats immediately instead of after 30 seconds
description: The tray stats thread sleeps 30 seconds before its first query, so menu items show 'Memories: —' for up to half a minute after launch.
evidence:
.spawn(move || loop {
    std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_secs(30));
suggestion: Run the refresh body once before entering the sleep loop.

title: Only hide the window on tray click when it is focused
description: toggle_main_window hides whenever is_visible() is true. A visible but unfocused window gets hidden by left-click instead of brought to front — opposite of toggle intent.
evidence:
match window.is_visible() {
    Ok(true) => { let _ = window.hide(); }
suggestion: Hide only when is_visible() && is_focused(); otherwise show and focus.

title: Send GUI tracing console output to stderr instead of stdout
description: init_logging attaches a tracing layer to std::io::stdout. Today MCP transport lives in a separate binary so protocol stream is safe — but any future in-process stdio use, or piping GUI stdout, interleaves log lines with data output. stderr is conventional for diagnostics.
evidence: .with_writer(std::io::stdout),
suggestion: Switch console layer to std::io::stderr.

title: Log resume_pending failures instead of discarding them
description: `let _ = operations::resume_pending(state_arc.clone());` discards the Result. If recovery fails (locked DB, IO error), queued operations silently never resume and nothing reaches logs.
evidence: let _ = operations::resume_pending(state_arc.clone());
suggestion: Match on error and tracing::error! it with context.

title: Fail gracefully at startup instead of panicking on expect
description: setup() uses expect() for app_data_dir and AppState::open, run() ends in expect(). A corrupted DB or unresolvable path makes the app crash-loop invisibly on macOS release builds (no console, no dialog), and no custom panic hook routes panics into the log file.
evidence:
let data_dir = app.path().app_data_dir().expect("app data dir resolvable");
let mut state = AppState::open(&data_dir).expect("open app state");
suggestion: Install a panic hook logging to file appender; convert startup failures into user-visible dialog / clean non-zero exit.

title: Preserve SQLite error codes in BiError::Db
description: From<rusqlite::Error> flattens to e.to_string(), discarding sqlite error code. Callers cannot programmatically distinguish UNIQUE violations from BUSY/READONLY, so surfaces emit raw strings and cannot map to friendly actionable messages.
suggestion: Carry e.sqlite_error_code()/extended code alongside message in Db variant.

title: Validate bit_width instead of truncating with as u8
description: create_project reads bit_width as u64 then casts with `as u8`: values above 255 wrap silently (300 becomes 44) and unsupported widths flow unchecked into index quantization config, producing confusing downstream behavior instead of clear input error.
evidence: bit_width: args.get("bit_width").and_then(|v| v.as_u64()).map(|n| n as u8),
suggestion: Use u8::try_from(n).ok() and validate against supported bit-width allowlist.

title: Surface .biTurbo marker write failures in create_project
description: After inserting the project row, failure to write the .biTurbo marker swallowed with `let _ =`. If root_path doesn't exist or isn't writable, project created without marker and later root_path-based resolution silently falls back to default project — hard-to-diagnose isolation breakage. create also never checks root_path exists, unlike ensure_marker_files.
suggestion: Propagate write error (or log) and validate root_path.is_dir() at create time.

title: Purge recall_feedback rows when deleting a project
description: delete removes memories and project row but leaves recall_feedback rows whose memory_uid belonged to deleted memories. Orphaned feedback accumulates unboundedly across project lifecycles keeping stale ranking signals.
evidence:
tx.execute("DELETE FROM memories WHERE project_id = ?1", ...)?;
tx.execute("DELETE FROM projects WHERE id = ?1", ...)?;
suggestion: Delete feedback for the project's uids within same transaction.

title: Support or cleanly reject JSON-RPC batch requests
description: A top-level JSON array (JSON-RPC batch, permitted by MCP 2024-11-05 revision advertised) fails deserialization into JsonRpcRequest and is answered with single -32700 parse error instead of per-entry responses.
suggestion: Deserialize to Value; on Array dispatch each element and reply with array — or explicitly reject batches with -32600.

title: Fail loudly when SCHEMAS_JSON drifts from implemented tools
description: tool_schemas() silently degrades to empty tools list if embedded JSON fails to parse — every client would see zero tools. Additionally 7 implemented handlers absent from SCHEMAS_JSON (intentional per 27-tool note) but nothing asserts advertised set matches dispatcher, so future drift invisible.
suggestion: Panic or log error on schema parse failure; add unit test asserting every advertised tool has a call_tool arm.

title: De-flake smoke tests: model dependency and fixed 3s windows
description: Every smoke test opens full AppState (fastembed BGE embedder) and polls filesystem with fixed 200ms sleeps inside 3-second deadlines. On cold machine model must be present/downloaded before search works; on slow CI the 3s window can elapse before debounced flusher fires — flaky failures unrelated to regressions.
suggestion: Use stub/deterministic embedder for tests or derive completion from observable flush events; make timeouts generous/configurable.

title: Share one app-identifier constant between MCP server and GUI
description: run_mcp_server_stdio hardcodes dirs::data_dir().join("com.biturbo.app"), duplicating identifier from tauri.conf.json. If bundle identifier ever changes, GUI and MCP server silently operate on different datasets.
suggestion: Export pub const APP_IDENTIFIER from biturbo_lib and use in both.

title: Do not fall back to CWD for the data dir in the MCP binary
description: dirs::data_dir().unwrap_or_else(|| PathBuf::from(".")) makes the binary open/create com.biturbo.app under whatever directory the agent launched it from when OS data dir unavailable — silently splitting state and scattering logs into unrelated working directories.
suggestion: Exit with clear error when OS data dir cannot be determined instead of falling back to '.'.

title: Remove tracked vite.config.js that shadows vite.config.ts
description: A compiled copy of vite.config.ts is committed AND git-tracked (verified via git ls-files: vite.config.js, vite.config.d.ts, tsconfig.tsbuildinfo, tsconfig.node.tsbuildinfo all tracked). Vite resolves config files in order vite.config.js -> vite.config.mjs -> vite.config.ts, so `vite`, `vite build`, and `tauri dev` load the .js file and silently ignore edits to vite.config.ts. `npm run build` (tsc -b) re-emits the .js so the build path self-heals, but `npm run dev` alone uses the stale copy — a config edit diverges silently in dev. Root cause: tsconfig.node.json is composite with no noEmit, so tsc -b emits JS+DTS+tsbuildinfo into repo root; .gitignore lists these files but they were committed before being ignored.
evidence: .gitignore lists vite.config.d.ts / vite.config.js / tsbuildinfo — yet `git ls-files` reports all four as tracked; tsconfig.node.json sets "composite": true with no noEmit.
suggestion: git rm --cached vite.config.js vite.config.d.ts tsconfig.tsbuildinfo tsconfig.node.tsbuildinfo; stop emitting by dropping composite/references and typechecking with tsc --noEmit.

title: Set a Content-Security-Policy instead of csp: null in tauri.conf.json
description: The webview ships with CSP fully disabled. Tauri's security model treats the CSP as core defense-in-depth: with csp null, any HTML/script injection into the webview (biTurbo renders arbitrary agent/user-authored memory content and ingested code chunks) executes with full access to Tauri IPC and plugin permissions — including the unscoped fs read/write grants in capabilities/default.json. No dangerouslySetInnerHTML sink exists today, so this is hardening rather than open RCE, but the blast radius of any future rendering bug is total.
suggestion: Define a strict CSP (default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; connect-src ipc: http://ipc.localhost; img-src 'self' asset: data:) relying on Tauri's automatic nonce/hash injection.

title: Revoke unused over-granted fs/shell/process/updater capabilities
description: The only frontend plugin imports in src/ are plugin-dialog (Projects.tsx) and plugin-autostart (Settings.tsx); no plugin-fs/shell/process/updater usage anywhere in the webview (updater driven from Rust via UpdaterExt which needs no capability). fs:allow-read-text-file and fs:allow-write-text-file are granted WITHOUT scope objects, meaning the webview IPC surface can read/write arbitrary user-writable paths. Combined with csp:null this is pure attack surface with zero current functional benefit.
evidence:
"fs:default",
    "fs:allow-read-text-file",
    "fs:allow-write-text-file",
    "fs:allow-read-dir",
    "fs:allow-exists",
    "shell:default", ...
suggestion: Delete the fs/shell/process/updater permission entries (keep dialog, autostart, core:*), or add explicit scope objects.

title: Make ensure-sidecar-placeholder detect and refresh stale placeholder sidecars
description: The script writes the 11-byte text 'placeholder' but afterwards can never distinguish that placeholder from a real binary. If a build is interrupted between placeholder creation and the cargo/copy step, or a user follows docs/release.md troubleshooting before running a direct `tauri build`, the text file gets bundled as the biturbo-mcp externalBin and shipped — MCP tools then fail at spawn with cryptic exec-format/JSON errors. Nothing validates the bundled sidecar before packaging.
suggestion: Read existing file: if content equals 'placeholder' (or size below sanity threshold), rewrite and warn; add post-copy sanity check in build-sidecar.mjs.

title: Build the MCP sidecar in run-wsl-cuda.mjs rebuild path
description: rebuild() runs `npm run build`, drops only a text placeholder, then builds just `cargo build --bin biturbo`. The biturbo-mcp sidecar is never compiled nor staged next to target/release/biturbo — this optimized WSL CUDA flow produces an app whose MCP server is missing (or a stale placeholder), breaking all MCP tools. Secondary: needsRebuild() scans src/, index.html, package.json, vite/tailwind configs but not public/, so changed public assets never trigger a dist rebuild.
evidence:
await run("node", ["scripts/ensure-sidecar-placeholder.mjs"]);
await run("cargo", ["build", ..., "--bin", "biturbo"]);
suggestion: Also build --bin biturbo-mcp and copy to target/release (or call build-sidecar.mjs); include public/ in the mtime scan.

title: Isolate MCP test harnesses from the production data directory
description: mcp-smoke-test.ts (npm run mcp:test), recall-eval.ts and seed-memories.ts spawn biturbo-mcp with no environment override, and biturbo_mcp.rs hardcodes dirs::data_dir()/com.biturbo.app — every test run creates/deletes projects and memories in the user's real store, the same SQLite DB the GUI has open. Cleanup is success-path-only: delete_project runs inside try{} before finally, so any failed assertion, timeout, or crash leaves orphaned smoke-*/eval projects polluting real data.
evidence: this.proc = spawn(bin, [], { stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "pipe"] });  // no env/data-dir isolation
suggestion: Support a BITURBO_DATA_DIR override in biturbo_mcp.rs, spawn harnesses with fresh mkdtemp dir, move cleanup into finally blocks.

title: Guard release.yml workflow_dispatch from tagging a branch name
description: tagName derives from github.ref_name. On a manual workflow_dispatch run (documented in docs/release.md as the way to test the pipeline), ref_name is the branch name (e.g. 'main'), so tauri-action tries to create a draft release tagged 'main' containing binaries whose embedded version matches nothing.
evidence: tagName: ${{ github.ref_name }}
suggestion: Add a workflow_dispatch `tag` input validated against refs/tags/v*, or skip release upload unless github.ref starts with refs/tags/.

title: Purge committed tooling artifacts (.opencode dylibs, tsbuildinfo, session state)
description: git ls-files confirms ~9.4MB of tooling junk committed: seven ~896KB x86_64 macOS dylibs under .opencode/tmp/ plus a V8 node-compile-cache blob tree (useless on any other machine), the two tsconfig*.tsbuildinfo caches, vite.config.d.ts, and AI-tool state files (.omo/run-continuation/ses_*.json session continuation — potentially private conversation data, .cursor/hooks/state/*.json, .mavis/plans/*). Bloats every clone, creates spurious diffs/merge conflicts, leaks local tooling/session state. None covered by .gitignore.
evidence: du -k .opencode/tmp/.*.dylib → 7 × 896KB; git ls-files tracks .opencode/*, .omo/run-continuation/ses_*.json, .cursor/hooks/state/*.json, .mavis/plans/*, tsconfig*.tsbuildinfo, vite.config.d.ts.
suggestion: git rm -r --cached .opencode .omo .mavis .cursor '*.tsbuildinfo' vite.config.d.ts and add these patterns to .gitignore.

title: Pick one package manager — package-lock.json and pnpm-lock.yaml are both tracked
description: Two independent dependency-resolution sources committed: package-lock.json (used by CI's npm ci) and pnpm-lock.yaml, alongside pnpm-workspace.yaml. Contributors who install with pnpm update only pnpm-lock.yaml; CI then installs a stale tree from package-lock.json (or fails once it drifts out of sync with package.json). The repo mixes manager idioms: bun-style trustedDependencies, 'pnpm mcp:build' comments, npm everywhere else.
evidence: git ls-files → package-lock.json AND pnpm-lock.yaml both tracked; ci.yml `run: npm ci`; package.json has "trustedDependencies".
suggestion: Standardize on npm end-to-end (delete pnpm files) or commit to pnpm and switch CI/scripts; document in README.

title: Enforce version sync across package.json, Cargo.toml, tauri.conf.json
description: release.mjs reads only package.json and tags v<version>; it never verifies src-tauri/Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, or tauri.conf.json. docs/release.md instructs manually bumping six files — miss one and the GitHub release ships v0.3.0 assets whose app self-reports the old tauri.conf.json version, so the updater endpoint keeps offering the same 'new' release forever and version checks lie. release.yml likewise never validates tag↔version agreement.
evidence:
const pkg = JSON.parse(readFileSync("package.json", "utf8"));
const tag = `v${version}`;  // no comparison with src-tauri manifests
suggestion: Before creating the tag, parse all four manifests and hard-fail on mismatch (or auto-sync them).

title: Add frontend test/lint infrastructure and enforce it in CI
description: Rust gets fmt + clippy -D warnings + cargo test in CI, but the React 18/Zustand frontend has zero tests, zero linting, and no tooling installed (no vitest/eslint in devDependencies; no test/lint scripts). Frontend regressions — store logic, the entire api.ts invoke layer, view behavior — are caught only by TypeScript compilation. For an app whose product is trustworthy memory storage, the UI half ships with no safety net.
evidence: scripts: { dev, build, preview, typecheck, tauri*, mcp:*, recall:eval, release } — no test or lint entry; ci.yml frontend coverage is just `npm run build`.
suggestion: Add vitest + eslint with test/lint scripts wired into ci.yml; start with unit tests for lib/store and lib/api.

title: Compress the 4.9MB public/logo.png used as favicon
description: public/logo.png is 5,134,912 bytes and is referenced as the document favicon in index.html. Vite copies it verbatim into dist/, so every installer ships a 4.9MB file the webview downloads at startup to render a ~32×32 tab icon — roughly 25× larger than the actual app icon (196KB). Pure waste in bundle size, disk, and startup I/O.
evidence: stat(public/logo.png) = 5134912 bytes; index.html:5 <link rel="icon" type="image/png" href="/logo.png" />
suggestion: Generate a small favicon set (32/64px PNG or .ico, ≤50KB) and move full-resolution logo out of public/.

title: Drop nonexistent landing/ package from pnpm-workspace.yaml
description: The workspace declares a `landing` package but no landing/ directory exists anywhere in the repo. Depending on pnpm version this either fails install or silently no-ops; stale config that misleads contributors.
evidence:
packages:
  - "."
  - "landing"   ← directory does not exist
suggestion: Remove the - "landing" entry until the package exists.

title: Sync .biturboignore with .gitignore (missing src-tauri/binaries/)
description: .biturboignore says it was 'created from .gitignore on first ingest' but has drifted: .gitignore ignores src-tauri/binaries/ (sidecar placeholders and multi-MB biturbo-mcp binaries) while .biturboignore only excludes src-tauri/target/ and src-tauri/gen/. biTurbo's own ingest will chunk and embed binary sidecar files into semantic memory, polluting search results and wasting index space.
evidence:
src-tauri/target/
src-tauri/gen/     ← .gitignore additionally lists src-tauri/binaries/
suggestion: Regenerate .biturboignore from current .gitignore; ideally derive it at ingest time instead of maintaining a frozen copy.

title: Typecheck scripts/*.ts harnesses in CI
description: Eight TypeScript dev harnesses execute via node --experimental-strip-types, which strips types without checking them. No tsconfig includes scripts/ (root includes only src; tsconfig.node.json only vite.config.ts) and CI never typechecks them, so type errors accumulate silently until a harness crashes mid-run.
evidence: "include": ["src"], "references": [{ "path": "./tsconfig.node.json" }]
suggestion: Add tsconfig.scripts.json (noEmit, include scripts) plus a typecheck:scripts npm script wired into ci.yml.

title: Cache cargo builds, parallelize smoke job, cancel superseded CI runs
description: Every CI run compiles the full Rust dependency tree from scratch — the rust job has no Swatinem/rust-cache (release.yml does, so the omission is inconsistent), and the mcp-smoke job uses needs: rust, serializing behind it and compiling everything again with no cache. No concurrency group, so pushed commits queue redundant full runs; no dependency-audit gate.
evidence:
jobs:
  rust:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest   ← no rust-cache step; mcp-smoke: `needs: rust`; no `concurrency:` block
suggestion: Add swatinem/rust-cache@v2 to both jobs, drop needs: rust, add concurrency with cancel-in-progress, consider scheduled audit job.

title: Self-host fonts instead of fetching Google Fonts at every launch
description: The local-first desktop app preconnects to and downloads Fraunces/Inter/JetBrains Mono from fonts.googleapis.com on every window load. Offline — a primary scenario for a local memory tool — brand fonts fail silently and fall back, shifting layout; online, every launch leaks a request to Google, contradicting the local-first privacy positioning.
evidence: <link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com" />
suggestion: Vendor the three families as woff2 (fontsource packages or committed files), declare @font-face locally, drop external links.

title: Add LICENSE file promised by README badge and package.json license field
description: The README badge links to ./LICENSE and the footer says 'MIT.', but no LICENSE file exists in the repo (verified via git ls-files), and package.json has no license field. Without a license the code is 'all rights reserved' by default — contradicting the badge and legally blocking the reuse/forks the README invites.
evidence: [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-8FB87D.svg)](./LICENSE)   → ./LICENSE is not tracked
suggestion: Commit the standard MIT LICENSE text and add "license": "MIT" to package.json.

title: Fix release docs: pipeline builds NSIS .exe, not .msi
description: docs/release.md's build table claims the Windows release artifact is a .msi installer, but release.yml passes --bundles nsis, producing NSIS setup .exe files. README's Windows section similarly points readers at bundle/msi paths. Anyone following the docs looks for the wrong artifact name.
evidence: | Windows x64 | `windows-latest` | `.msi` installer |   vs release.yml: args: "--bundles nsis"
suggestion: Update docs to say NSIS .exe, or add msi to the release bundles.

title: Replace unmaintained fs2 and drop tokio 'full' feature bloat
description: fs2 is flagged unmaintained in the RustSec advisory DB (recommended successor fs4 offers the same FileExt API used for the cross-process write lock in db.rs). Separately, tokio's features = ["full"] pulls every optional subsystem into both the GUI binary and the MCP sidecar when only a small subset is needed — slower clean builds and larger binaries.
evidence:
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["full"] }
fs2 = "0.4"
suggestion: Migrate db.rs to fs4 (drop-in FileExt), narrow tokio to features actually used (rt-multi-thread, macros, sync, time).
